about: The `annual_report_catalogue` table, published whole. See /api/schema for its grain. This file is fy 2020 only.

rows.name: Table of contents
rows.what_it_is: Two-page contents list mapping every department and report section to its page range, and naming the boards that filed nothing ('No Report Submitted': Agricultural Commission, Cultural Council, Green Community Task Force, Housing Authority).

rows.notes: The listed page numbers are reliable EXCEPT for the election section: the contents say 'Special State Primary Election March 3, 2020 ... 188-191' and 'Presidential Primary Election March 3, 2020 ... 192-195', but page 188 holds the Special State Primary AND a Special State Election, and pages 189-191 already hold Presidential Primary results, which are then reprinted on 192-195. See surprises.

rows.name: General fund appropriations summary and classification of accounts, FY2020

rows.notes: THE SINGLE MOST VALUABLE TABLE IN EITHER DOCUMENT, and it extracted with columns aligned -- a stark contrast with FY2019, where the equivalent table is unusable. Caveats: some cells are OCR-corrupted, especially on page 30 ('577,163.0' for $77,163.00, '- 2000', '5202600', '3047000', '830,3000', '51.770,967.83', '541,024,362.4'), and where a value is blank in the source the row is short. Note the GRAND TOTAL of $43,104,912.84 here is LARGER than the omnibus budget voted for the year, because this table includes carry-forwards, transfers to other funds and state/county assessments.

rows.name: Finance Committee: FY2021 budget reductions from target
rows.what_it_is: The departments and plans cut to build the COVID-era FY2021 budget, each with the dollar reduction, inside the Finance Committee's narrative.
rows.layout: Indented bullet list inside prose.
rows.printed_total: reductions leave a $1,055,950 surplus; total requested budget appropriation $38,658,115
rows.notes: COVID CONTENT. Lunenburg Public Schools $192,157; Capital Plan $664,333; DPW $102,000; Additional Firefighter $95,359; Additional Police Officer $84,664. The surrounding prose gives further hard figures: revenue projections down $300,290 from the pre-COVID budget; school budget 57% of town expenses at $22,029,972 including the Monty Tech assessment plus $1,076,000 in other school-related costs; state aid down 1.1% ($78,483 less) while the school assessment rose 5.85% ($356,763) and Monty Tech 0.92% ($88,131); FY2021 new growth estimated at $173,400; the town's debt ratio 'evaluated as poor by an independent agency'; and the OPEB allocation re-allocated to the stabilization fund. This page is the clearest single statement in either report of what COVID did to the town's finances.

rows.name: FY 2021 capital plan (original January recommendation)

rows.layout: Six columns, one project per line.
rows.printed_total: Total Capital Plan $1,329,133; Funding: Raise & appropriate $650,000, Free cash $679,133, Unexpended Capital (blank), Premium Reserved for Capital (blank), Total $1,329,133
rows.notes: COVID CONTENT AND A GOOD EXAMPLE OF THE PANDEMIC CHANGING A NUMBER MID-YEAR. The page prints the ORIGINAL January plan of $1,329,133 and then explains in prose that on 16 April the Town Manager told the committee the $650,000 tax-funded portion would have to be deferred to a fall Special Town Meeting; the committee re-voted a revised plan of $664,800 using $14,333 less free cash. The revised list itself is NOT printed here -- the town meeting record on p150 shows $647,880 was actually voted in June and p168 shows a further $494,333 voted in November. Four different figures for the same year's capital plan appear in this one report ($1,329,133 / $664,800 / $647,880 / $494,333) and they must not be confused.
